2. It is stated that respondent No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the suit for a decree of partition for a share of 1.07 acres of land out of the suit land measuring 3,22 acres of land fully described in the schedule to-the plaint. 

 14. A person who wants to make construction must have a clear title on the land. If one is allowed to make multistoried construction on land which he purchased in excess of the share of a co-sharer, then in the event of decree in the suit, partition of such multi-storied building would thereby unnecessarily be made difficult. Moreover, it would not be just and equitable to allow such purchaser to make construction on such excess land until final adjudication of the shares of the co-tenants. In the circumstances, the impugned order of status quo does not call for any interference. The appeal accordingly fails.
